pages.summary: A line added to the current axes, without clearing them.
body: Unlike `plot`, `line` is a low-level function: it adds to the axes as they are, whatever hold says, and takes no line spec, only names and values. It gives the line object when asked.

examples.title: Lines added to a plot

pages.summary: Functions plotted from text or handles, the older way.
body: `ezplot` plots f(x) over an interval (-2 pi to 2 pi unless given), or an implicit curve f(x, y) = 0; `ezplot3` a curve x(t), y(t), z(t) in 3-D (t from 0 to 2 pi), marking its end with `'animate'`; `ezpolar` a curve r = f(theta) in polar axes. The functions are text such as `'cos(t)'` or function handles. `fplot`, `fimplicit`, `fplot3` and `fpolarplot` are the newer forms.

examples.title: Three older plots
examples.code:
subplot(1, 3, 1), ezplot('x^2 - 2', [-2 2])
subplot(1, 3, 2), ezplot3('cos(t)', 'sin(t)', 't/5', [0 4*pi])
subplot(1, 3, 3), ezpolar('1 + cos(t)')

title.string: x = cos(t), y = sin(t), z = t/5

pages.summary: Markers in 3-D, and scatter plots with points of the same x spread sideways.
body: `scatter3` places markers at points in 3-D, with sizes and colours of their own. `swarmchart` spreads the points of each x sideways so that they do not hide each other: by density (wider where they are many, the default), at random (`'rand'`), or not at all; `swarmchart3` spreads in x and y.
syntax: s = swarmchart(x, y, sz, c, 'filled', 'XJitter', 'density', 'XJitterWidth', w)
s = swarmchart3(x, y, z, sz, c)

examples.title: Three groups as a swarm, and a cloud in 3-D

pages.summary: Bubbles at points, their areas growing with a size; in 2-D, 3-D and polar axes.
body: The smallest size in the axes gets the smallest bubble and the largest the largest: `bubblesize` sets their diameters in points (1 and 20 to begin with), `bubblelim` the sizes they stand for (the data's range unless set). Colours are one for all, a row for each bubble, or values through the colormap; the faces are partly see-through, so that overlapping bubbles show.

examples.title: Cities as bubbles

pages.summary: Bars sideways and in 3-D, and bars in order with their running percentage.
body: `barh` draws horizontal bars; `bar3` and `bar3h` bars as blocks in 3-D (a matrix's columns side by side, or `'grouped'` and `'stacked'`). `pareto` sorts bars from the largest down and draws their cumulative percentage over them, on a second axis: which few causes make up most of the total.

examples.title: Faults by cause

pages.summary: Histograms the older way, of two variables, and of angles.
body: `hist` draws a histogram of y in nbins bins (10), or with outputs gives the counts and the bin centres without drawing. `histogram2` bins pairs of values on a grid and draws the counts as bars in 3-D. `rose` is an angle histogram in polar axes (`polarhistogram` is the newer form).

examples.title: Counts, a joint histogram and directions

body: `fill` and `fill3` draw polygons from the columns of x, y (and z), each filled with a colour (or interpolated from colours at its vertices), clearing the axes unless held. `patch` adds a polygon object to the axes as they are, from points or from faces and vertices (as `isosurface` gives), with properties such as `'FaceColor'`, `'FaceAlpha'` and `'EdgeColor'`.

examples.title: A hexagon, a coloured triangle, a see-through square
examples.code:
t = (0:5)*pi/3;
fill(cos(t), sin(t), [0.3 0.6 0.9]), axis equal, hold on
patch([1.5 3 2.2], [-1 -0.5 1], [1 2 3])
patch('Faces', [1 2 3 4], 'Vertices', [0 -0.5; 2 -0.5; 2 0.5; 0 0.5], 'FaceColor', 'r', 'FaceAlpha', 0.3)
hold off

pages.summary: Markers in polar coordinates, polar axes, and the older polar plot.
body: `polarscatter` places markers at angles theta (radians) and radii rho, with sizes and colours of their own. `polaraxes` makes polar axes (angles round a circle, radii out from the middle), alone or in a tile of `subplot`, with properties such as `ThetaZeroLocation`, `ThetaDir` and `RLim`. `polar` is the older form of `polarplot`.

examples.title: Wind directions and speeds, north at the top, clockwise

pages.summary: Arrows in 3-D, from the origin, and along an axis.
body: `quiver3` draws an arrow from each point (x, y, z) along (u, v, w), scaled so that they do not overlap unless the scale is 0 or `'off'`. `compass` draws arrows from the origin in polar axes, one for each pair (U, V) or complex number; `feather` draws them from evenly spaced points along the x-axis, a time series of directions.
syntax: quiver3(x, y, z, u, v, w, scale)

examples.title: Normals of a surface, and a day's wind

pages.summary: Stems in 3-D, columns as ribbons, and a pie in 3-D.
body: `stem3` draws stems from z = 0 up to each value, with markers at their ends; `ribbon` draws each column of Y as a ribbon of a width (0.75); `pie3` draws a pie chart as a solid.

examples.title: Three 3-D charts
examples.code:
[X, Y] = meshgrid(1:5);
subplot(1, 3, 1), stem3(X, Y, exp(-((X - 3).^2 + (Y - 3).^2)/4), 'filled')
subplot(1, 3, 2), ribbon(peaks(20))
subplot(1, 3, 3), pie3([3 2 1], [0 1 0])

pages.summary: The path of a point, with its head.
body: The path is drawn with a marker at its end, the point's position at the last time. Here it is drawn whole at once: the figure shows the path as it ends.

examples.title: A spiral's path

pages.summary: A line that points are added to as a program runs.
body: An animated line starts empty (or with points); `addpoints` adds points, drawn at the next `drawnow`, the oldest dropped beyond `'MaximumNumPoints'`; `clearpoints` takes them all off; `getpoints` gives them. It takes a line's properties, so that colour, width and markers can be set.

examples.title: A trace that keeps its last 50 points

pages.summary: Lines and shaded bands across the whole axes.
body: `xline` draws vertical lines at x values and `yline` horizontal ones, reaching across the axes whatever the limits become and not changing them, with a line spec and labels. `xregion` and `yregion` shade bands between pairs of values. Each gives its objects, whose `Value` moves them.

examples.title: Limits and an interval marked

pages.summary: Two plots with a y axis each, the older way.
body: The first plot uses the left axis and the second the right, both sharing x; each may be drawn by its own function (`'plot'`, `'semilogy'` and the like). The outputs are both axes and both plots. `yyaxis` does the same in steps.
syntax: [ax, h1, h2] = plotyy(x1, y1, x2, y2)
[ax, h1, h2] = plotyy(x1, y1, x2, y2, fun1, fun2)

examples.title: A temperature and a pressure

pages.summary: Graphs and trees drawn from matrices and parent lists.
body: `gplot` draws an edge for each nonzero A(i, j) between the points in rows i and j of xy (or gives the lines' coordinates). `treelayout` gives positions for drawing a tree from its parent list (parent(k) is node k's parent, 0 for a root): leaves evenly across, each parent above its children. `treeplot` draws the tree; `etreeplot` the elimination tree of a sparse matrix.

examples.title: A ring of six, and a small family tree
